colorado.climate_classification: Continental Alpine (Cold, shallow-to-medium snowpack, persistent weak layers)

himalaya.climate_classification: Mixed Monsoon-Influenced Transitional to Dry High-Altitude Cold Desert (Karakoram / Ladakh)
himalaya.station_density: Sparse / Valley-Confined (Mountain telemetry stations spaced 40-100km apart)

covariate_shifts.impact: Atmospheric pressure, lapse rates, and solar radiation are substantially different. Colorado elevation features cannot be directly transferred without recalibration.

covariate_shifts.colorado_range: Continental winter storms (Pacific jet stream moisture, relatively low density snow)
covariate_shifts.himalayan_range: Western Disturbances (WD) in NW Himalaya + Monsoon incursions in Central/Eastern Himalaya
covariate_shifts.impact: Storm precipitation totals during Western Disturbances can produce 50-150cm snow in 48h, far exceeding typical Colorado storm rates. Model weights learned on Colorado would severely underestimate storm loading risks in the Himalayas.

covariate_shifts.colorado_range: Median distance to SNOTEL: ~2.5 km (High density)
covariate_shifts.himalayan_range: Median distance to IMD/DGRE AWS: ~45-80 km (Sparse valley network)
covariate_shifts.impact: IDW spatial interpolation in Himalaya requires a wider search radius (65km vs 35km) and higher uncertainty penalty.
Extreme relief generates massive avalanche paths with runout distances exceeding 3-8 km, requiring distinct path modeling.

implications_for_modeling: 1. Direct Cross-Domain Transfer is Scientifically Invalid: Applying a Colorado-trained model directly to Himalayan coordinates will suffer catastrophic domain shift.
2. Independent Calibration Required: Probability distributions cannot be shared across domains.
3. Zero-Fallback Policy is Essential: When Himalayan telemetry or models are unavailable, the system must return INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than using Colorado predictions.
4. Domain-Isolated Spatial Interpolation: IDW must strictly forbid mixing SNOTEL stations with Indian mountain stations.
